source_refs.note: Exercise 3.4, Question 9: Exercise 3.4, book page 94: Q1-Q15 (integration by partial fractions); answers book pages 301-302

blocks.explanation:
Denominator mein do qisam ke factors hain: \(x - 2\) jo ek dafa aata hai, aur \((x + 3)^2\) jo repeated hai. Is liye yeh Case-II hai.
Teen constants chahiye: \(x - 2\) ke liye ek, aur \((x + 3)\) ki dono powers ke liye ek ek.
Plan: roots \(x = 2\) aur \(x = -3\) se \(A\) aur \(C\), phir \(x^2\) ka coefficient compare kar ke \(B\), aur aakhir mein integral.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(\int \frac{25(x + 2)}{(x - 2)(x + 3)^2}\,dx\).
Maloom karna: yeh integral.
Tareeqa: partial fractions, Case-II. Fraction proper hai (upar degree 1, neeche degree 3). Upar wala 25 sirf ek constant hai, ghabrane ki baat nahi; bas numbers bare aayenge.

Partial fractions likhein
\[\dfrac{25(x + 2)}{(x - 2)(x + 3)^2} = \dfrac{A}{x - 2} + \dfrac{B}{x + 3} + \dfrac{C}{(x + 3)^2}\]
\[25(x + 2) = A(x + 3)^2\]
\[+\, B(x - 2)(x + 3) + C(x - 2) \quad (1)\]
Kyun: Repeated factor \((x + 3)^2\) ke liye power 1 aur 2 dono ke fractions. Phir poore denominator se multiply: \(A\) ke saath \((x + 3)^2\) bacha, \(B\) ke saath \((x - 2)(x + 3)\), aur \(C\) ke saath sirf \((x - 2)\).

(1) mein \(x = 2\) aur \(x = -3\) rakhein
\[x = 2:\ 100 = 25A,\ A = 4\]
\[x = -3:\ -25 = -5C,\ C = 5\]
Kyun: \(x = 2\) par left side \(25 \times 4 = 100\) aur right side par sirf \(A(5)^2 = 25A\). \(x = -3\) par left side \(25 \times (-1) = -25\) aur sirf \(C(-5)\) bacha.

\(x^2\) ke coefficients compare karein
\[0 = A + B\]
\[B = -4\]
Kyun: \(B\) ke liye koi aisa root nahi jo baaqi sab ko zero kar de. Right side kholein to \(x^2\) sirf \(A(x + 3)^2\) aur \(B(x - 2)(x + 3)\) se aata hai: \(A + B\). Left side \(25x + 50\) mein \(x^2\) hai hi nahi.

Integral lein
\[\int \left(\dfrac{4}{x - 2} - \dfrac{4}{x + 3} + 5(x + 3)^{-2}\right)dx\]
\[= 4\ln|x - 2| - 4\ln|x + 3| - \dfrac{5}{x + 3} + c\]
\[= 4\ln\left|\dfrac{x - 2}{x + 3}\right| - \dfrac{5}{x + 3} + c\]
Kyun: Pehle do terms \(\ln\) dete hain. Teesra term power rule se: \(5\int (x + 3)^{-2}\,dx = 5\cdot\frac{(x + 3)^{-1}}{-1} = -\frac{5}{x + 3}\). Aakhir mein \(4\ln|p| - 4\ln|q| = 4\ln\left|\frac{p}{q}\right|\).
Dhyan dein: \(\frac{5}{(x + 3)^2}\) ka integral \(5\ln(x + 3)^2\) nahi hai; \(\ln\) sirf power 1 par aata hai.

Tasdeeq (constant term)
\[9A - 6B - 2C = 36 + 24 - 10 = 50 \;\checkmark\]
Kyun: (1) ke right side ka constant term: \(A \cdot 9 + B \cdot (-6) + C \cdot (-2)\). Left side ka constant \(25 \times 2 = 50\). Dono barabar, is liye teeno constants sahi hain.

blocks.text: Kitab ke aakhir mein answers (page 302) mein Exercise 3.4 ke jawab ghalat heading "Exercise 3.6" ke neeche chhape hain. Is sawal ka jawab us block ka item (ix) hai: \(4\ln\left|\frac{x - 2}{x + 3}\right| - \frac{5}{x + 3} + c\). Yeh jawab sahi hai. Jis block par "Exercise 3.4" likha hai (page 301) woh kisi aur exercise ke jawab hain, is liye wahan se milane ki koshish na karein.
